title: A Drop for the Safehouse
premise: Astrid Vasquez, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 447, has spent a decade hiding inside the Witness Protection-adjacent network that saved her from testifying about what she found in the wreckage. When the safe house she shares with two other protected witnesses is listed for sale online — with interior photos revealing their faces, their routines, their hiding places — Astrid realizes someone inside the program is selling them out. Racing to stop a staged 'accident' meant to erase all three of them before a reopened inquiry can hear her testimony, Astrid must choose between the rules that kept her alive and the makeshift family she's built. In the end she trades her anonymity for the truth, testifying under her real name and dismantling the corrupt handler who sold them — finding that identity, once surrendered, is the only thing worth dying to reclaim.
about_author: Felix Vane is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent eight years reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction full-time. Writing from a coastal town they refuse to name, Vane specializes in thrillers where bureaucracy is the most dangerous antagonist of all.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ten years after losing her family in row twelve, Astrid works crash sites for the NTSB while living off-grid in Safehouse 7 with Marek, a whistleblower accountant, and June, a former translator. The chapter establishes her ritual of reading the passenger manifest every anniversary. Emotional beat: grief worn smooth into routine.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: June's POV. June finds Safehouse 7 on a real estate site — twelve photos, interior shots showing Marek's medication bottles, June's books, Astrid's wall of flight diagrams. Someone photographed them living. Panic fractures the house's fragile peace as they debate who to call when the only people who know the address are the ones protecting them. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of safety.

chapters.title: Protocol Ghosts
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid contacts her handler, Delacroix, who insists the listing is a database error and orders them to relocate per protocol. But the relocation route he assigns passes directly through a tunnel with a history of 'accidents.' Astrid, professionally fluent in how accidents are manufactured, starts pulling old case files. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into certainty.

chapters.title: What Marek Knew
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek confesses why he's really in protection: his ledgers implicated Meridian Logistics, a contractor whose trucks appear in three 'accidental' crashes — including, possibly, Flight 447's ground servicing crew. The trio realizes their cases are one case. Emotional beat: three lonely wars becoming one shared front; found family forged in confession.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: June's POV. The safe house protocol manual arrives by courier with new pages — rules rewritten to isolate them, stagger their movements, cut communications. Astrid recognizes the handwriting of control: someone is engineering their separation before the scheduled hearing where Astrid is set to testify. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Delacroix
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid confronts Delacroix at a diner, playing the obedient witness while recording him. He slips — references the tunnel, mentions Meridian's 'insurance problem.' Leaving, she spots the tail car she was told wouldn't exist. She must decide whether to run alone or trust Marek and June with the truth. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: Split Routes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Following the rewritten protocol, they're moved to separate transit — exactly as designed. June's bus is diverted; Marek's escort turns down the tunnel road. Astrid, having refused her own route, races back toward the safe house carrying the one piece of evidence that matters: Marek's original ledger page. Emotional beat: terror at maximum velocity.

chapters.title: The Tunnel
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The staged accident begins — brake failure engineered, a Meridian truck positioned as the innocent cause. Marek survives because he never boarded the car, watching from the trees as it goes over the embankment without him. He now holds proof the attack happened and photographs of the crew. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt inverted into purpose.

chapters.title: Everything Loud
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. At the reopened inquiry, with Delacroix's men closing in, Astrid chooses exposure over invisibility: she takes the stand under her real name, enters the ledger, the recording, the tunnel photos, and names Meridian and its protector inside the program. The room erupts; federal agents arrest Delacroix mid-extraction. Emotional beat: ten years of silence breaking open into testimony.

chapters.title: A House With Windows
chapters.summary: June's POV, resolution. Months later, the three of them rent an ordinary house with curtainless windows — no protocols, no aliases, faces visible to the world. Astrid visits a new memorial wall and finally adds her family's names aloud instead of in silence. Found family becomes simply family. Emotional beat: grief integrated, identity reclaimed, home chosen rather than assigned.
